_doc: Batch m13 (medium, opus themed pass): fox kits, fennec, three hares (frost, mountain, jackrabbit), grumpy lemming, pika, marmot, glacier cub, reindeer calves. Motifs in motifs/medium_m13.js; every creature has its own signature motif with its own chain effect. Shared inside the batch: hare-hind-kick (frost hare, mountain hare, jackrabbit: the same big hind foot in three palettes and layouts). The hares share one side-view drawing routine so they read as relatives. Distinct from the small snowshoe-leveret-dash (snow-print) and lemming-kit-scurry (fury-tuft).

fox-kit-pair.notes: Two fluffy russet fox kits from a tundra den, all big dark-tipped ears and white muzzles: they never stop play-fighting, pouncing on each other, nipping ears and tumbling.

u0.n: Den Wall: den mouths line the edge, two pairs of ear tips and bright eyes peering out of each dark arch

p.u1: Pair Pounce: the two kits crouch, pounce out of the edge one on top of the other and drop back

u2.n: Kit Cover: bushy white-tipped tails curl out of the edge and fluff up into a soft hedge

u3.n: Practice Bite: a kit nips its sibling's ear tip and tugs as they launch off the edge, a tiny yelp mark

p.b0: Playful Paw Swat: kit pairs bounce off the edge one after another, one pouncing on the other

b1.n: Mock-Fight Tumble: one tumbling pair of kits rolls the length of the edge

b2.n: Kit-Tumble Guard: the kits curl nose in tail along the edge, white tail tips breathing

p.b3: Playground Barge: a kit pair barges out of the edge shoulder first and drops back

fennec.notes: A tiny pale desert fennec that is mostly ears: two huge pink-lined ears swivel to hear prey under the sand; it hunts at night, digs in a blink and sleeps curled in its burrow.

u0.n: Night Snap: a fennec runs the length of the edge under a moon glint, ears pricked forward, and snaps

u1.n: Burrow Nap: a fennec curls up with its ears folded flat and its tail over its nose; Zs rise as it mends

u2.n: Sand Curtain: digging forepaws fling fans of sand out of the edge, the fennec gone behind them

u3.n: Ear Warning: the ears snap up at spots along the edge, listening arcs spreading from both tips

p.b0: Big-Ear Scratch: big-eared fennec faces launch off the edge one after another, ears swivelling

b1.n: Dune-Top Ambush: sand bursts off the edge as the fennec drops out of the dune top

b2.n: Ear-Tuned Hunch: fennec faces hunch along the edge, listening arcs pulsing from the ear tips

p.b3: Dune-Edge Shoulder: a fennec shoulders out of the edge and drops back, a sand ripple behind it

frost-hare.notes: A white tundra hare with black ear tips and frost in its fur: it bounds in huge arcs leaving Y-shaped tracks, jinks in zigzags, thumps a warning and breathes frost.

u0.n: Hare Kick: big white hind feet kick straight out of the edge one after another, snow puffing where they strike

u1.n: Zigzag: white hares jink left and right in sharp zigzags out from the edge and back, snow kicked up

u2.n: Thump: a hind foot stamps flat at spots along the edge, shock rings spreading over the snow

u3.n: Frost Breath: twitching noses breathe frost rings that bloom out of the edge with an ice crystal, then pull back

p.b0: Frost-Paw Rake: white hares bound off the edge and land in frost sprays

b1.n: Winter Gust Bash: a frost breath gusts out of the edge and drops back

p.b2: Drift Hunker: white hares hunker in a row along the edge, black ear tips up, snow sifting on them

b3.n: Snowy Haunch Shove: a haunch and big hind foot shove out of the edge and drop back, snow puffing

mountain-hare.notes: A grey-brown hill hare with long ears and big pale feet: it lies pressed into its form (a scraped hollow) all day, grazes clover at dusk and naps in its hollow; when it runs it lopes uphill.

u0.n: Hill Kick: one big pale hind foot kicks the length of the edge, a puff where it strikes

u1.n: Clover Graze: three-leaf clovers along the edge are nibbled away, the green bits rising as it mends

p.u2: Form Hide: the hare lies pressed into its scraped hollow along the edge, ears flat, grass tufts round it, eye blinking

u3.n: Hollow Nap: a round loaf of hare naps in its hollow, ears folded along its back; it rises breathing slow with a Z

b0.n: Hill-Paw Raking: loping hares launch off the edge, big pale feet raking

b1.n: Hill-Den Mauling: a hare lopes out of the edge, mauls and drops back

b2.n: Hollow Mending Crouch: napping hare loaves line the edge, breathing slow

b3.n: Sleepy Haunch Shove: a sleeping loaf of hare shoves out with its haunch and drops back, still asleep

jackrabbit.notes: A lean, long-legged desert jackrabbit with enormous ears that glow pink with red veins in the sun: it sprints low and straight, hides in thorny scrub with only the ear tips showing.

u0.n: Long Leg Kick: a long hind leg shoves out of the edge in a straight kick and drops back, dust where it lands

p.u1: Ear Flick: huge sunlit ears flick off the edge one after another, pink with red veins

u2.n: Scrub Hide: thorny grey-green scrub bristles out of the edge, two tall ear tips twitching behind it

u3.n: Straight Back: a lean jackrabbit at full stretch sprints straight down the length of the edge, dust behind

b0.n: Zigzag Scrabble: lean jackrabbits scrabble off the edge, dust off their hind feet

b1.n: Sail-Ear Slap: a huge ear swings out of the edge and slaps back

b2.n: Scrub-Dodge Stance: scrub bushes line the edge, ear tips twitching behind them

b3.n: Doubled-Back Barge: a jackrabbit doubles back and barges out of the edge, dust flying

grumpy-lemming.notes: A round black-capped tundra lemming that is always cross: scowling brows, puffed cheeks, bared buck teeth, a little storm cloud of a mood; it digs into the snow to sulk and stares you down.

u0.n: Grumble: little dark storm clouds blink at spots along the edge, muttering a rumble zigzag and dripping rain

p.u1: Lemming Bite: scowling lemmings fly off the edge teeth bared, an anger mark popping

u2.n: Dig Snow: lemmings dive head first into snow out from the edge, bums up, flinging snow chunks, then come back

u3.n: Sulk Stare: narrowed slit eyes glare from fur balls at spots along the edge, red glare dashes reaching out

b0.n: Furious Paw Swipe: scowling lemmings fly off the edge, angry marks popping

b1.n: Stubby Fury Clout: a cross lemming shoves out of the edge, clouts and drops back

b2.n: Grumble Hunch: little storm clouds sit along the edge muttering, rain dripping

b3.n: Cross Lemming Shove: a glaring fur ball shoves out of the edge and drops back

pika-sentry.notes: A round grey-brown pika with round ears and no tail, sitting sentry on a boulder in the scree: it calls a sharp eep, pitches stones and carries mouthfuls of hay and flowers to its haypile.

p.u0: Warning Whistle: pikas pop out of the edge calling eep, call marks flying, and drop back

u1.n: Stone Pitch: lichen-spotted scree stones are pitched off the edge one after another, spinning

u2.n: Hay Rampart: bunches of hay stalks and flower heads bristle out of the edge like a little rampart

u3.n: Sentry Stand: pikas sit on lichen-spotted boulders along the edge, turning their heads left, front, right

p.b0: Scree Paw Slap: pikas launch off the edge paw first, scree pebbles rattling

b1.n: Thrown Scree Hurl: stones lobbed off the edge fall away spinning

b2.n: Sentry Ready Stance: pikas sit round along the edge, ears up, calling now and then

b3.n: Alarm Whistle Shove: a pika on its rock shoves out of the edge and drops back

marmot-bruiser.notes: A fat, summer-fed golden marmot that stands tall with a dark face mask and pale belly: it whistles alarms, shoves turf about and simply drops its whole weight on things.

u0.n: Marmot Slam: marmots belly-flop off the edge one after another, dust puffing out both sides

u1.n: Ground Shove: slabs of turf shoved by fat paws hang at spots, a crack opening behind each, tied in a tripping line

u2.n: Whistle Warn: standing marmots whistle sharply and scatter out from the edge, white whistle marks flying, then come back

p.u3: Fat Crush: a fat marmot stands tall, shoves out of the edge and drops its whole weight into a squashed sit
p.b0: Fat-Belly Cuff: fat golden marmots launch off the edge belly first

b1.n: Summer-Fed Crush: a belly flop shoves out of the edge and drops back with a dust thud

b2.n: Fat Roll Bulwark: flattened marmots line the edge like sandbags

b3.n: Bruiser Body Check: a turf slab is body-checked out of the edge and drops back

glacier-cub.notes: A small round blue-white cub of the glacier with frost crystals on its crown: it belly-slides on the ice, skids on all fours and fluffs itself into a frosty fur ball.

u0.n: Cub Pounce: a round blue-white cub bounds the length of the edge and pounces, frost glinting on its crown

u1.n: Ice Slide: cubs skid out from the edge on splayed legs, ice chips spraying, and skid back

u2.n: Fur Fluff: cubs puff into round fur balls out from the edge, frosty tufts bristling, then settle back

u3.n: Glacier Belly Slide: belly-sliding cubs hang at spots, tied together by their ice streaks in a tripping line

b0.n: Moraine Swipe: cub faces launch off the edge, moraine grit thrown

b1.n: Frost Cuffing: frosty fur balls fly off the edge one after another

b2.n: Frosted Pelt: fluffed frosty fur balls line the edge, tufts turning

b3.n: Gnome-Bowl Slide: a belly-sliding cub bowls out of the edge and slides back

reindeer-calf-herd.notes: A small herd of fuzzy brown reindeer calves with two velvet antler buds each and cream muzzles: they huddle rump to rump in the snow, butt with their buds, bleat for each other and trot with clicking knees.

u0.n: Calf Huddle: calves huddle rump to rump along the edge, warm breath steaming up

p.u1: Herd Screen: calf faces push out of the edge velvet buds first and hold like a soft fence

u2.n: Antler Bud Butt: a calf lowers its head and butts out of the edge with its velvet buds, then drops back

u3.n: Herd Bleat: calf muzzles bleat, soft arcs and warm breath rising as the herd mends

p.b0: Antler-Bud Jab: calf faces jab off the edge one after another, heads lowering

b1.n: Fuzzy-Knob Butt: one calf trots the length of the edge head down and butts at the end

b2.n: Huddle Wall: a wall of huddled calves holds the edge, breath steaming

b3.n: Huddle Shuffle: the huddle shuffles out of the edge and back, steaming
